reason: This text fragment (Exodus 2:1-10) narrates the birth of Moses and contains only incidental references to 'Hebrews' and 'Hebrew women.' The passage is entirely set in Egypt under Pharaoh's authority (Pharaoh's daughter, the Nile River). There is no portrayal whatsoever of the Hebrews as a nation possessing or having their own specific land. Rather, the narrative implicitly depicts Hebrews as a subject people living under Egyptian jurisdiction.
